messages:
maya: infra-bot alerted: Xid79 spike on rack-r12 (us-east1) ~ 02:10 UTC, lots of short-lived sessions. seen 23 Xid79s in 10m :warning:
infra-bot: alert details -> metric:gpu.xid.79.count=23, host=rack-r12-node-7, model=realtime-embedder, tenant=tenant-42
samir: can someone paste dmesg from that node?
kevin: grabbing it now, looks like repeated DMA faults. dmesg snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=21456, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568120] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=21458, GPU panic: recovery failed
```
kevin: nvml shows ECC correctable counts spiking on GPU2, also dma engine errors. `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,DRIVER,PERFORMANCE`
maya: tenant-42 is low-latency embeddings, tiny batches (~1-2) at high concurrency. hypothesis: many tiny kernels + frequent memory churn exposing flaky card or DMA race.
elaine: cross-checking NIC logs — saw a brief 100ms RX stall on node-7's 10gbe link around same time. possible interplay with PCIe or driver stack.
samir: interesting. Xid79 commonly means GPU detected memory or bus fault; pairing with NIC stalls could cause driver timeouts. we should correlate timestamped traces (xid, dmesg, pcie errors, net)
ops-bot: trace links -> https://ops.redwood/sessions/1769987600-1769987700/node-7 (collected logs + perf counters)
maya: quick mitigations: 1) soft-drain node-7 2) move tenant-42 to reserved pool (dedicated-short) for 1h 3) disable preemption for that rack to avoid runaway requeues
kevin: soft-drain commands:
```
kubectl cordon node-7
kubectl drain node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```
kevin: also set NV driver watchdog to collect full GPU dump before reboot: `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 2` (but careful on prod)
elaine: vendor diag suggests run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and collect /var/log/messages + dmesg right after drain.
samir: longer term: tag GPU2 for warranty replacement (ID: SN-A10-7-02) if we see repeat failures post-reboot. provisioning cost check: replacing a noisy A10 vs shifting tenant to A100 reserved — which is cheaper short-term?
maya: rough numbers: A10 replacement RMA covered under warranty for this fleet. A100 reserved burst cost ~ +$1.8k/mo for pool reservation but improves throughput and reduces tail latency. for 1-2 hour mitigation, routing to existing A100 pool is cheaper.
onchalant reaction: @oncall - can you own the soft-drain and routing change?
oncall: on it, starting drain now. will post updates. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: drain started at 1769987689, evicted 12 pods, 2 pods failed to reschedule (stateful).
kevin: note: make sure we annotate node-7 with `gpu-health=investigate` so autoscaler won't reprovision into same rack automatically.
maya: post-action plan: 1) repro on node in staging with synthetic tiny-batch workload + NIC perturbation 2) run vendor stress test for 24h 3) open RMA if fail persists 4) policy: auto-migrate tenants with >10 Xid warnings within 15m to dedicated pool
elaine: created incident ticket INC-2026-314 in ops-tool, linked logs, assigned to hardware team.
samir: good. I'll start the correlation notebook (xid vs small-batch qps vs nic rx_stall) and share plots. expected ETA 4h.
maya: thanks everyone. update thread when RMA or repro result available. :sparkles:
